title: I want to study film. Where do I start?

commenti.body: On writing, beyond Syd Field, Vogler or Campbell’s bibliography, I strongly recommend “Story” by Robert McKee, I loved that book and made me appreciate and understand narratives way more. Regarding cinematography basics, “The Bare Bones Camera Course for Film” is a jewel. For Directing, “Shot by Shot” by Katz gives several examples of visualizing a scene, with multiple storyboard examples. Finally, if you want a general book that covers several topics, “The Filmmaker’s Handbook” by Ascher is a quintessential bible.

Start with these books. They're probably the definitive entry texts into film art/history

The History Of Narrative Film by David Cook

Film Art by David Bordwell and Kristin Thompson

How To Read A Film by James Monaco

Film Theory And Criticism by Leo Braudy and Marshall Cohen

For technical aspects:

The Filmmaker's Handbook by Steven Ascher and Edward Pincus (general filmmaking)

In The Blink Of An Eye by Walter Murch (editing)

The Five C's Of Cinematography by Joseph Mascelli (cinematography)

Cinematography: Theory And Practice by Blain Brown (deeper cuts on technique)

Making Movies by Sidney Lumet (directing)

Adventures In The Screen Trade by William Goldman (screenwriting)

The internet is a Wild West of self-professed "experts" and "authorities." And because of that you'll be swimming in an ocean of competing "do it my way" conflicting chest-thumping.  But Film Riot and Filmmaker IQ are generally comprehensive.

Finally, take a gander at [Sight & Sound's Top 250](https://www.bfi.org.uk/sight-and-sound/greatest-films-all-time).  It's the more definitive list of greatest films/directors out there. Cuts a diverse and inclusive path. Pay less attention to the rankings and look at it as an overall body of films.  Also, this place - [TSPDT Top 1000](https://www.theyshootpictures.com/gf1000_all1000films_table.php) in fantastic.

Whoa, okay, thank you. This is incredible. 

What would be the most comprehensive starting text? I'll be reading one at a time, of course. :)
I'd start with the History Of Narrative Film by  Cook.  It pretty much covers everything.
Thanks. This is excellent. I'll be looking into your other recommendations as well.
